---
title: "1:n-1 does not go from 1 to n-1"
ref: NUM-12
categories: [Numbers]
impact: silencieux
extrait: '1:5-1'
reponse: '0 1 2 3 4'
attendu: "`1 2 3 4`"
versions: "All"
source: "The R Inferno"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
n <- 5
1:n-1
-2^2
```
:::

## Why

The `:` operator takes precedence over addition and subtraction. `1:n-1` therefore reads as `(1:n) - 1`: R builds 1 to 5, then subtracts 1 from each element.

Likewise, the power comes before the unary minus: `-2^2` reads as `-(2^2)` and gives -4. That is the mathematical convention, but it is surprising when you think "minus two, squared".

## The remedy

Add parentheses as soon as `:` or `^` sits next to another operator.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
1:(n - 1)
(-2)^2
```
:::
